criteria.text: Patients identified as high risk for colon cancer are eligible for continued screening every 24 months.

criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-007, cov-009 to cov-012, cov-014, cov-022 to cov-026, cov-032, cov-033, doc-001.
criteria.text: Colonoscopy to investigate symptoms or findings is covered for: an imaging abnormality likely to be significant; unexplained bleeding (blood in the stool not thought to be from a rectal or perianal source, black tarry stool of unknown origin, or a positive stool blood test); unexplained iron-deficiency anemia; significant unexplained diarrhea with other findings such as weight loss; examining the whole colon for synchronous cancer or polyps in a patient with a treatable cancer or polyp; chronic inflammatory bowel disease when a more precise diagnosis or the extent of activity will change immediate management; locating during surgery a lesion that cannot be found by touch or sight; acute colonic ischemia; Streptococcus bovis endocarditis; unexplained new-onset constipation that does not respond to medical treatment; an anorectal adenomatous polyp; or infectious colitis.

criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-013, cov-015, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-021.
criteria.text: Surveillance is covered for a history of colorectal cancer or polyps, follow-up one year after colorectal cancer surgery, follow-up after removal of a large sessile adenoma (more than 2 cm in its greatest dimension), and inflammatory bowel disease surveillance (pancolitis for more than 7 years, or left-sided colitis for more than 15 years; not for disease limited to the rectosigmoid).

criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-036 to cov-039, cov-041 to cov-049.
criteria.text: Colonoscopy is generally not covered, unless the record documents why it is needed, for: chronic, stable irritable bowel syndrome or chronic abdominal pain (in unusual cases it may be done to rule out organic disease, especially when symptoms do not respond to therapy); acute diarrhea; hemorrhoids; routine follow-up of inflammatory bowel disease (cancer surveillance in Crohn's disease or chronic ulcerative colitis excepted); routine examination before elective abdominal surgery for a non-colonic disease; upper GI bleeding or black tarry stool with a demonstrated upper GI source; or bright red rectal bleeding with a convincing anorectal source on sigmoidoscopy and no other symptoms suggesting a source higher up. It is also generally not covered for fulminant colitis, possible perforation, acute severe diverticulitis, or diverticulosis as the reason for the test (it may still be reported when it is the final diagnosis).

Visited for routine evaluation at Podiatry Associates on 11/03/2026. 30-year-old male with a 2 cm ulcer on his right heel extending to the fat layer, seen one on one. This visit was to address wound care, with a focus on off-loading, infection control, and blood-sugar management to facilitate wound closure. This is the fourth debridement since 07/31/2026 when sharp debridement was last performed; the ulcer has significantly reduced in size each week. The patient's previous care plan was reviewed and revised last week. 

The patient has a history of hyperlipidemia managed with statin therapy, hypothyroidism controlled with levothyroxine, and vitamin D deficiency being supplemented. He also has a past medical history of a kidney stone treated in 2008 with no recurrence. Currently, he takes a multivitamin, loratadine, fish oil, calcium carbonate, levothyroxine, and is allergic to penicillin without rash since. 

The patient is a former smoker who quit years ago, lives alone, and is independent at home. He works in an office setting, has no fever, chills, unplanned weight loss, urinary symptoms, changes in vision, chest pain, palpitations, cough, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, or change in bowel habits. His mood is stable, he sleeps well, and has no recent changes in his review of systems. 

Assessment included a psychiatric review showing the patient to be alert, oriented, with a normal mood and affect. Physical exam found an abdomen that was soft, nontender, nondistended with normal bowel sounds. An after-visit summary was printed for the patient. 

Patient portal access was reviewed, and a copy of this note was sent to the referring clinician. The patient came alone to the visit and understands how to reach the clinic for any questions. No prior hospital admissions were reported. The patient has no recent psychiatric concerns. 

Plan: Selective removal of dead tissue from the open wound, aiming to limit the initial debridement to 20 square cm or less. Off-loading strategies will be reinforced. Instructions for home care will include continued wound cleaning and daily application of a new dressing material selected for its debridement properties. Follow-up in two weeks to reassess the wound's progress.

criteria.text: Active wound care (debridement) is covered to remove dead tissue and promote healing, performed with direct one-on-one patient contact, following accepted standards of wound treatment.

Care must be part of a plan that addresses complicating factors (pressure off-loading, infection, poor circulation, metabolic or nutritional problems), aiming at wound closure or, when healing is not possible, preventing the wound from getting worse.

How often debridement is done depends on the wound. When the goal of care is healing, a given type of wound care is not continued if the record does not show improvement leading to healing, and when the expected healing is not documented after 30 days the plan of care should be revised. When the goal of care is not healing, the patient is managed under palliative care standards.

criteria.text: Extremity ultrasound is covered to detect cysts, abscesses, tumors (including their size) or effusions, or to tell solid tumors from fluid-filled cysts; to evaluate tendons, joints, plantar fascia, ligaments, soft-tissue masses, ganglion cysts, intermetatarsal neuromas or metatarsal stress fractures; or to help diagnose and remove foreign bodies.

received.clinical_notes: 19y/o female, wound clinic f/u. Removed dead tissue from 2cm ulcer on right heel down to fat layer; 1:1 with pt. Care plan: off-loading, infection control, blood-sugar mgmt for wound closure. Wound care ongoing for 10wks. Smoker history (qtd yrs ago), asthma (inhaler as needed), hyperlipidemia (statin), occ constipation. Current meds: albuterol inhaler, multivitamin, loratadine, omeprazole. Allergic to sulfa (hives). Works as accountant, non-smoker, drinks socially, lives with family. ROS: neg for fever, chills, weight loss, urinary sx, vision changes, chest pain/palps, cough/SOB, nausea/vomit, bowel habit change, mood, sleep. Assessment: non-pressure chronic ulcer R heel & midfoot (L97.412), nicotine dependence (Z87.891), uncomplicated asthma (J45.909). Procedure: selective removal of dead tissue from open wound (first 20sq cm or less). No admissions, hospitalizations, surgeries, etc. to report. No recent tests or results. No relevant family or social history to report. Dizzy spells addressed during visit with history, exam, treatment plan.
